meta.name: Community and governance
meta.about: How HAX is run, generated from the governance files in the unified issue queue: roles and succession, the four steps every decision goes through, the documents every repo keeps, and the places people meet.

cg_contributors.desc: Anyone who files issues, submits pull requests, reviews, writes docs or translations, or helps on Discord. Maintainership is earned through contribution, not granted by affiliation; six months inactive and a maintainer is thanked and can return the same way.

cg_discord.desc: The HAXTheWeb Discord: real-time help and discussion. Decisions made here are written back to an issue.

billrose.note: Backup owner: the second name in every CODEOWNERS file; takes over merges and releases if the primary maintainer is away.

bryan.note: Primary maintainer: holds the * slot in every CODEOWNERS file, merges, cuts releases and breaks ties.

psu.note: Institutional steward: employs the primary maintainer, holds the copyright and keeps the infrastructure going.

cg_d1.desc: Anyone can open an issue in the unified queue; it is the single source of truth for the whole ecosystem.

cg_d2.desc: Discussion happens on the issue. Larger work gets a written plan as a comment, labeled Plan Created.

cg_d3.desc: Work lands as a pull request that says which issue it fixes, through CLA, CodeQL and review.

cg_d4.desc: Breaking changes are called out on the issue and in release notes; decisions made on Discord or in person are written back to an issue.

cg_governance.desc: Roles, how decisions are made, the maintainer lifecycle, succession, conflicts of interest and a yearly governance review. In webcomponents, haxcms-nodejs, haxcms-php, create, praw, issues.

cg_contributing.desc: How to contribute: an issue first, then a pull request that says which issue it fixes. In webcomponents, haxcms-nodejs, haxcms-php, create, praw, issues.

cg_conduct.desc: The code of conduct every space follows. In webcomponents, haxcms-nodejs, haxcms-php, create, praw, issues.

cg_security.desc: How to report a vulnerability privately, and the incident response that follows (INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md). In webcomponents, haxcms-nodejs, haxcms-php, create, praw, issues.

cg_support.desc: Where to get help: Discord, the documentation, then the unified issue queue. In webcomponents, haxcms-nodejs, haxcms-php, create, praw, issues.

cg_sustain.desc: How HAX is resourced: Penn State employment and student interns, hosting partnerships, grants and community contributions; what free support covers. In webcomponents, haxcms-nodejs, haxcms-php, create, praw, issues.

cg_trademark.desc: How the HAX name and marks may be used. In webcomponents, haxcms-nodejs, haxcms-php, create, praw, issues.

cg_agents.desc: Rules for AI agents and people working in each repo: lint, precheck and the conventions the code keeps. In webcomponents, haxcms-nodejs, haxcms-php, create, issues.

cg_cla.desc: Apache-2.0 plus a contributor license agreement; CLA Assistant runs on every repo and signatures live in haxtheweb/cla. In webcomponents.

scenes.caption: A primary maintainer, a backup owner, Penn State as steward, and contributors.
1. Open an issue. Anyone can open an issue in the unified queue; it is the single source of truth for the whole ecosystem.
2. Discuss and plan. Discussion happens on the issue. Larger work gets a written plan as a comment, labeled Plan Created.
3. Pull request. Work lands as a pull request that says which issue it fixes, through CLA, CodeQL and review.
4. Record it. Breaking changes are called out on the issue and in release notes; decisions made on Discord or in person are written back to an issue.
The rules, in writing, in every repo.
Where people meet: Discord, Learn HAX, HAX Camp and the issue queue.
